free_tier.stated: No free tier. V6-1 is USD 0.49 a month: 1 CPU core, 2 GB RAM, 20 GB NVMe, one IPv6 address plus a /64, no IPv4 and no NATed IPv4, KVM. Billed yearly, so the shop prints USD 5.88 annually. The V6-2 rung doubles RAM and disk for USD 0.99 a month, USD 11.88 a year.

retention.stated: yearly prepay; the shop lists orders, renewals, invoices and cancellation in the billing panel. No deletion grace period is printed on any page read.

egress.terms: the bandwidth table prints 'V6-1 - Not limited' and 'V6-2 - Not limited'; no byte figure and no shaping threshold is published
egress.free_allowance: not limited, per the vendor's own table

interface_detail: KVM guest with Linux install options from the billing panel; the plan carries a /64 as well as a single address, so a listener can bind any port on any address in the prefix. There is no IPv4 at all, and no NAT layer.
tooling: any SSH client over IPv6; a host without IPv6 needs a tunnel or a dual-stack jump host to reach it, which the vendor does not supply
chaining: 2 GB of RAM for USD 0.49 a month is the most memory per dollar found in the band, but it is reachable only over IPv6, so it is a WireGuard node for a client that already has IPv6 or a monitor that reports outward

limits.value: bandwidth 'Not limited' with no published threshold; the vendor reserves the right to act on abuse
no IPv4 at all: 'These servers do not include IPv4 connectivity or NATed IPv4 access', so there is no port-forwarding layer and every port on the /64 is reachable
yearly prepay: USD 5.88 is the first payment, not USD 0.49

binding_note: IPv6-only is the constraint that decides the whole row: a WireGuard peer without IPv6 cannot reach it at all, and no IPv4 add-on is offered on this plan.

identity_cost.detail: a billing-panel account; the order page and registration form were not reachable through the text extractor or the headless browser, so the fields are not read. No card hold is stated anywhere read. Payment is '3D Secure Credit Cards - Visa, MasterCard, etc.', Bitcoin and several altcoins, Alipay, and WebMoney Z / MIR cards per the vendor's knowledge base, so a debit card on the 3-D Secure rail should work.

notes: The best shape per dollar in the band by a wide margin and the least usable of the cheap rows. 2 GB and 20 GB for USD 0.49 a month is four times the RAM of the next cheapest NAT row and 0.23 of the per-GiB price of the C-Servers row (USD 0.245 a GiB against USD 1.06), and because there is no NAT layer, every port on the /64 is reachable, so the port-mapping problem that governs the other NAT sellers does not exist here. The price is IPv6: no IPv4 address, no NATed IPv4, and the vendor offers no add-on, so a WireGuard peer on an IPv4-only access network cannot reach it. Two things pull the confidence down. The stock count on the order page read '0 Available' for both rungs at the Poland datacenter, so the row is priced and documented but not demonstrably in stock today. And the entity needed correcting: the vendor names BREEZLE LLC of Brandon, Florida, but a Florida entity search returns no such company, while the RIPE organisation record for the AS the vendor claims gives 'reg-nr = 4921432 (Delaware)' - so the entity is a Delaware LLC mailing from a Florida address, the Florida register is the wrong place to look, and the Delaware number was not checked against the Delaware register. That is a real entity with a real AS and a domain-age story, not the dissolved-company pattern was warned about, but it is also not a completed registry check. Not established: the registration form's fields, the payment gateway list at checkout, the renewal price after year one, and whether stock exists at any location.

extras.price_arithmetic: USD 0.49 a month x 12 = USD 5.88 a year, which is the figure the shop prints. A VPS bills whether it runs or not, so the 24/7 and 10 h/day figures are the same. The V6-2 rung is USD 0.99 x 12 = USD 11.88.
